All ports are on the FRONT in TWO BANKS of sixteen stacked columns, and the columns are GANGED IN FOURS - four shells of four columns per bank, with a 4.13 mm gutter between them. Two 25G SFP28 in-band management cages, an RJ-45 management jack, a USB 3.0 Type-A storage port, an RJ-45 console, a ToD jack, 1PPS and 10 MHz timing jacks, six system lamps and a reset button share the right of the wall; two 3000 W supplies and FOUR fan trays are on the rear. Its twin edgecore/ais800-64d is the same chassis with a QSFP-DD800 wall - and the two walls are laid out differently, which is the whole reason this one was fitted from scratch: the 64D spreads sixteen columns on a single 24.019 mm pitch and puts one lamp on the post beside each cage, and this one gangs its columns and puts two lamps in the legend row above them.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Where edgecore/ais800-32o's port lamps are. That device records the same gap and this one does not close it, but it narrows it: THIS model's legend row is the same `N (up) (down) N+1` and it carries two lenses between the arrows, at the column centre +/-1.998 on a baseline of its own. The 32O's elevation, rendered at 600 dpi, leaves exactly that space blank while resolving the numerals and arrows either side of it at the same scale - so the silence there is a reading rather than a resolution limit, and the 32O either carries its lamps somewhere this model does not or its drawing omits them. Its own LED enlargement, or a photograph of its face at 5 px/mm or better, settles it. The front elevation's panel rectangle is 2230.26 x 444.96 px at 600 dpi by subpixel edge fit (56 top / 58 bottom / 24 left / 22 right samples): 2230.26/440 is 5.0688 px/mm and 444.96/87 is 5.1145, and the aspect 5.0123 against the real 5.0575 is 0.90% out. The rear reads 2226.33 x 440.84 - 5.0598 and 5.0671, 0.14% apart. THE DRAWINGS ARE UPSCALES AND THAT WAS CHECKED: the panel edges ramp over about eight pixels, so an edge carries about +/-4 px of placement, which is where the front's 0.9% comes from. THE GUIDE'S OWN ENLARGEMENT IS THE SECOND INSTRUMENT, not a photograph. The System LEDs/Buttons figure draws the last four columns and the whole management cluster at 15.0367 px/mm in y - three times the elevation - and its x scale was calibrated against the elevation's sixteen-column pitch fit, giving 14.9234 px/mm with residuals of 0.006, 0.011 and 0.006 mm on three aperture centres. Every number below that both instruments can see agrees between them: the row pitch to 0.000 mm, the aperture-row centres to 0.08, the lamp offset to 0.001 and the arrow offsets to 0.04."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"A QUICK START GUIDE AND A DATASHEET, AND THE DATASHEET IS SHARED WITH THE TWIN. Both are staged: ais800-64o-qsg (8 pages, bilingual, 59 kept figures) and ais800-64o-datasheet (5 pages, 11 kept figures), and the datasheet is titled \"AIS800-64O/AIS800-64D\" and carries both models' ordering tables. The guide carries the Overview elevations, its own System LEDs/Buttons enlargement, the FRU replacement figures and a Connect Power page; the datasheet carries the photographs, the ordering tables and the power ratings. THE WEIGHT DISAGREES, AND BY MORE THAN THE TWIN'S DID: the guide says 20.5 kg (45.19 lb) \"with 2 PSUs and 4 fans installed\" and the datasheet 21.5 kg (47.4 lb) \"with 2 PSUs and 4 fan modules installed\" - a full kilogram, where the 64D's two documents differed by 0.3. Both are recorded; 20.5 is used because the guide is the document that also carries the measured elevations, which is the rule the 64D set. The dimensions agree exactly: the guide reads \"440 x 649.2 x 87 mm\" and the datasheet \"44 x 64.92 x 8.7 cm\". FIVE PHOTOGRAPHS ARE STAGED at 960 x 700 - front, front-angled, rear and rear-angled. Over a 440 mm face that is 2.18 px/mm, too coarse to measure, but they confirm the block structure, the two lamps per column, the model name printed on the panel and the red PSU latches and tray bars of the front-to-back build."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 1 SFP pair (mgmt-inband-1/mgmt-inband-2). OSFP stacks are left as drawn (S7): the 32 OSFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-63/port-64)."},"the-legends":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE NUMERALS ARE ANCHORED ON THEIR INNER EDGE, NOT THEIR CENTRE, and that is measured rather than assumed. The upper bank numbers 1 to 32, so it carries both one-digit and two-digit numerals on one baseline. Across fifteen columns the left numeral's RIGHT edge sits at -7.047 from the column centre for one digit and -7.015 for two, and the right numeral's LEFT edge at +6.842 and +6.815 - a difference of 0.03 mm - while the CENTRES move from -7.600 to -8.357 and from +7.631 to +8.146, a difference of 0.76. The numerals hug the arrows and grow outward. Anchoring them all in the middle would put every one-digit numeral 0.76 mm inboard of where the panel prints it, which is a third of the cap height. `anchor-by-row` was added to expand.py for this, the way `dx-by-row` was added for the offsets; the enlargement confirms the inner edges at -7.090 and +6.714. CAP HEIGHT 2.2 on the elevation and 2.28 on the enlargement, so font-size 2.8. THE ARROWS ARE SILKSCREEN AND THE LENSES ARE NOT. The 64 `(up)`/`(down)` glyphs are solid white, the same white and crispness as the numerals they sit between, where every lamp on this face reads as a bright lens. This is the AIS800-32D's finding applied before the fact; see roc-ops/Portrayal#396, open on the EXP100 and EXP800 for the same marks. Arrow centres sit at -4.717 and +4.833 from the column centre on the elevation and -4.678 and +4.854 on the enlargement. THE SFP28 PAIR'S TWO ARE LAMPS, as on the twin: the guide's callout 3 points at the white band between the two cages and names it \"SFP28 LEDs: Green (link/activity)\"."},"the-management-cluster-is-the-twins":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE CLUSTER IS THE SAME HARDWARE AND ITS GEOMETRY IS CARRIED FROM edgecore/ais800-64d, WHICH MEASURED IT ON AN ENLARGEMENT - and this device's own elevation and its own enlargement were both checked against that before carrying it, rather than the carry being assumed from the twin's name. THE CHECKS. Independent detection of the bright verticals on this elevation puts the SFP28 pair's bezel at 398.485-412.855 against the 64D's recorded 398.45-413.20. This guide's own enlargement, at 14.9234 px/mm, puts the USB-A opening at 418.10-430.40 against the 64D's 418.09-430.58 - 0.18 mm - and this elevation independently puts it at 418.09-430.32. The SFP28 row pitch reads 15.64 here against 15.30 there, which is the one number that differs by more than half a millimetre and is also the one this elevation resolves worst. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN, confirmed on this device's own enlargement: two 25G SFP28 cages in one bezel whose middle band carries the pair's two lamps and is legended `1 (up) 25G (down) 2`; an RJ-45 MGMT jack tab-up with its own pair of corner lamps and a blue-tongued USB 3.0 Type-A beneath it legended `SS`; a CONSOLE RJ-45 tab-up and a ToD RJ-45 tab-down stacked below; two SMA timing jacks legended 1PPS and 10MHz; six system lamps legended LOC DIAG ALRM FAN PSU1 PSU2 and a reset button legended RST; and the Edge-core badge with `AIS800-64O` printed beside it. THE VENT FIELDS AROUND THE CLUSTER ARE CARRIED TOO and are the weakest thing on this face. The three large fields are this device's own - top, left and bottom, measured below - but the four small fields that thread between the cluster's jacks are the 64D's, because neither this elevation at 5.07 px/mm nor the hole-finder run over the enlargement separated them from the jack apertures around them. They are decor on a region proven identical, and they are recorded here as carried rather than measured."},"the-optical-wall":{"confidence":"measured","note":"FOUR GANGS OF FOUR COLUMNS PER BANK, AND THE TWIN'S WALL IS NOT LIKE THIS. Aperture runs scanned along each of the four rows and fitted to x = first + floor(i/4)*B + (i mod 4)*p give, on three rows that resolve all sixteen columns cleanly: first 20.533 / 20.533 / 20.499, B 97.0718 on all three, p 23.2279 / 23.2279 / 23.2427, with an rms of 0.028-0.035 mm and a worst residual of 0.060. THE SAME BLOCK PITCH TO FOUR DECIMAL PLACES ON THREE INDEPENDENT ROWS is what settles that the structure is real and not a reading artefact. 20.5165 / 97.0718 / 23.2353 are used; the gutter is B - 4p = 4.1306. A SINGLE PERIODIC FIT WOULD AVERAGE THE GUTTER AWAY - the AIS800-32O records the same trap, and the EXP100's autocorrelation lesson is the same thing one generation earlier. THE 32O'S NUMBERS ARE NOT THESE AND WERE NOT BORROWED. That model fits 96.7913 / 23.4243 on a 438.4 mm shell; this is 97.0718 / 23.2353 on a 440 mm shell. The structure is shared with the 32-port OSFP model and the numbers are this device's own. ROWS. The mean vertical profile through all sixteen column centres puts the four aperture rows at 12.341-25.398, 27.234-40.306, 48.273-61.320 and 63.171-76.211. The row pitch within a bank is 14.900 (upper) and 14.894 (lower) - 0.006 mm apart, which is one pitch, 14.897 - and the enlargement returns 14.897 from its own two rows. The bank pitch is 35.927. THE DRAWN OPENING IS 22.40 x 13.05 against std/osfp@1's registry 23.1 x 13.5, the same consistent bias the 32O (22.4) and the 64D's QSFP-DD (18.3 against 19.0) both record. THE REGISTRY APERTURE IS CENTRED ON THE DRAWN ONE rather than hung from its top edge, which is the 64D's review finding applied before the fact rather than after: centring splits the 0.45 mm surplus 0.225 either way and the two banks come out identical. EACH GANG IS ONE SHELL. The panel draws a bright rounded frame around each four-column block, 93.51 x 29.33 at x 8.53 + n*97.064, with thin bright walls between the columns inside it and dark panel in the gutters - a vertical profile down the gutter between gangs 1 and 2 finds no bright run at all, which is what says the shell stops there. THE INTER-ROW BAND IS DRAWN ON A BACKING RECT, for the reason vent-field-needs-backing-rect exists: panel pattern decor paints only its holes, and this band is BRIGHT. It is a single row of round perforations 1.84 mm tall between the two apertures of each gang - EIGHT bands, one per gang per bank, because the band belongs to the cage assembly. GASKET FINGERS ALONG THE TOP AND BOTTOM OF EVERY SHELL, not lamps - the AIS800-64D's finding, and the same trap. Autocorrelating the three shell edges that resolve gives 2.762 mm on all three, and they run the full width of each shell. THE INTER-BANK STRIP IS PLAIN METAL. Between the upper bank's shell bottom at 40.98 and the lower bank's shell top at 47.63 there is 6.65 mm of panel whose grey reads 87-97 against the 94 of the metal beside it and which contains no hole at all. The 64D's face and this one both leave it blank, and it would have been easy to fill with a vent field nobody measured."},"the-port-lamps-are-two-per-column-in-the-legend-row":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST DEPARTURE FROM THE TWIN. edgecore/ais800-64d puts one round window on the post 2.40 mm to the LEFT of each cage, level with its own aperture row. THIS FACE HAS NO POST LAMP. Each column's legend reads `N (up) (o) (o) (down) N+1` and the two lenses sit on the legend baseline between the arrows - above the column in the upper bank, below it in the lower. MEASURED TWICE AT THREE TIMES THE RESOLUTION AND THE TWO AGREE TO A THOUSANDTH. On the elevation the offset from the column centre is +/-1.998 mm (sd 0.030, n=62); on the enlargement it is +/-1.998 (upper) and +/-1.999 (lower), with separations of 3.995 and 3.999. The lamp baseline is 9.907 in the upper bank and 78.742 in the lower, each with a standard deviation of 0.004 mm or better across the enlargement's four columns. THE LENS IS ROUND AND ABOUT 0.98 MM. The enlargement gives 0.980 x 0.973 in the upper bank and 0.980 x 0.998 in the lower - round to within a fortieth of a millimetre, which is the check the skill asks for. common/led-dot@1 is 2.0 square and is seated on the measured CENTRES rather than the measured size, as the 64D's and the 32D's indicators are and for the same reason: the indicator vocabulary is what a reader compares across devices. OWNERSHIP WAS CHECKED THE WAY THE 64D'S WAS. Sweeping the whole 440 mm width on each legend baseline for lenses of that size finds 16 columns x 2 in the lower bank with ZERO strays, and the same in the upper with a single out-of-column hit at x 430.1 - which is a system lamp in the management cluster, not a port lamp. Sixty-four lenses, one per port, and nothing hanging off either end of either bank. LEFT LENS TO THE UPPER PORT, RIGHT TO THE LOWER, which is what the arrows say: the left lens sits beside `(up)` and the right beside `(down)`, and odd ports are the upper row. WHAT THE FOUR COLOURS MEAN IS THE PORT'S. The guide gives one legend - \"OSFP800 LEDs: Yellow (800G), Blue (400G), White (200G), Green (100G)\" - and there is exactly one window per port, so the lamp shows the port's negotiated rate. AND THIS SETTLES A GAP ON A DEVICE ALREADY IN THE LIBRARY, or narrows it: the AIS800-32O records `port-lamp-windows` as needs-drawing because \"whatever this model does it does somewhere else, and the drawing does not show where\". Its legend row is the same `N (up) (down) N+1` and its elevation leaves the space between the arrows blank while resolving the numerals and arrows either side of it. See the gap of the same name below; this device does not change that one."},"the-rear-is-the-same-drawing":{"confidence":"measured","note":"NOT \"the same as the twin's\" - LITERALLY THE SAME IMAGE FILE. Both guides' page-1 Overview figures were rendered at 600 dpi, both rear panels located by the same subpixel edge fit, and both land on IDENTICAL bounding boxes: x 2559.33-4785.67, y 2080.31-2521.15, to the hundredth of a pixel. Resampled to a common grid the two rears differ by a MAXIMUM OF ZERO GREY LEVELS over 2000 x 396 pixels. The front, by contrast, differs in 41.63% of its pixels and the two front panels are not even the same size (2230.26 x 444.96 here against 2222.82 x 441.66 there), which is what says the front artwork is independently drawn for each model and the rear is one file used twice. SO THE REAR IS CARRIED OVER, per roc-ops/Portrayal#310, and the 64D is the reference. AND BECAUSE SHARED ARTWORK IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THIS MODEL, the carry was checked against this device's OWN rear photographs, which are not shared: they show two stacked Lite-On 3000 W supplies with IEC C20 inlets and red release latches, four fan trays with red handle bars, the `(up) PSU1 (down) PSU2` legend, the earth symbol and two grounding screws on the left strip, and the numerals between the trays. That is the front-to-back build and it is what the rear elevation draws."},"the-vent-fields":{"confidence":"measured","note":"HONEYCOMB, AND THE PITCH IS THIS DEVICE'S OWN. Hole centres found in the top field across three rows give an x pitch of 3.614, 3.603 and 3.606 mm - agreeing to 0.011 - with a half-pitch stagger of 1.659 between adjacent rows and a hole about 1.92 mm across. The row pitch is 2.08. (The twin records 3.59 x 2.07, measured separately on its own drawing; the two stencils are evidently the same and the numbers were not copied.) THE FIELDS. Top 0.15-6.55 and bottom 80.10-86.65 run nearly the full width; the left field is a column 8.5 mm wide running between them. There is NO field between the two banks, which is measured and not assumed - see the optical-wall note. g.data-description: the sixty-four 800G OSFP800 ports, in TWO BANKS of sixteen stacked columns, and the columns GANGED IN FOURS - a 23.2353 mm in-block pitch, a 97.0718 mm block pitch and a 4.13 mm gutter between shells. Ports 1-32 are the upper bank, numbered down each column from 1 at the top left, and 33-64 the lower - odd ports the upper row of their bank and even the lower, as the panel's own `N (up) (down) N+1` legends say. The upper bank's legends are printed above it and the lower bank's below.
